description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a large language model’s response to external feedback, as presented in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.81 to 0.99 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines at 0.2 intervals. The “Final Accuracy” (blue line with circle markers and solid line) remains consistently high, hovering between approximately 0.90 and 1.0 across all initial confidence levels, with minor fluctuations and error bars indicating low variance. The “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and dashed line) starts around 0.55 at 0.81 initial confidence, dips slightly, then rises steadily to nearly 0.95 at 0.99, showing a positive correlation with initial confidence. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange line with diamond markers and dashed line) begins near 0.45, declines sharply to below 0.1 around 0.87–0.89, then recovers slightly before falling again to near 0.0 at 0.99, indicating that the model’s improvement from feedback diminishes as initial confidence increases. Error bars are present for all three lines, suggesting variability in measurements, particularly pronounced for Δ Accuracy at lower confidence levels.
